items.title: Uttar Pradesh government orders probe into RPNLUP Assistant Professor recruitment
items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has ordered a probe into the recruitment of 12 Assistant Professors at Dr Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLUP). The order was issued by Dinesh Singh, Special Secretary of the Justice Department. The committee comprises the Principal Secretaries of three State departments. It will be headed by M Devraj, Principal Secretary, Personnel and Appointments Department. MP Agarwal, Principal Secretary, Higher Education Department, and Uday Pratap Singh, Principal Secretary, Justice and Legal Advisory Department are the other two members. The committee has been directed to submit its findings within 30 days. RPNLUP had advertised 12 Assistant Professor (Law) posts in March this year. Interviews for the posts were held between July 22 and 30. According to a report , the State of Uttar Pradesh's Additional Law Remembrancer, also a member of the University's Executive Council (EC), had sought records and explanations from the University's Registrar on the recruitment process. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: Delhi court sends Swatantra Bhardwaj to judicial custody for a day in Jantar Mantar assault case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Sunday sent right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj to judicial custody (JC) for a day in the case related to alleged assault on the father of a Dalit student-activist during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protests at Jantar Mantar in July. Duty Magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court passed the order. According to a lawyer involved in the case, Bhardwaj was produced at the judge's residence through virtual conference (VC). Police asked him to be sent to JC for 14 days. However, since he was produced before the Duty Magistrate, Bhardwaj was sent to JC for a day. The request for additional custody will be decided by the concerned court on Monday. Bhardwaj was arrested from Uttar Pradesh yesterday. He has been booked for offence of assault and provisions under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act [SC/ST Act] and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act). Bhardwaj was initially booked only for the offences under Sections 115(2) (causing simple hurt) and 126(2) (wrongful restraint) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
